title: Scientific Ontology (SO) / 存在境界論: Public Edition v4.3.0
description:
Scientific Ontology (SO) / 存在境界論 Public Edition v4.3.0 develops the boundary-oriented research movement established in the preceding public edition.

The release connects three layers of boundary cognition: critique of the conditions under which cognition is formed, formation of cognitive axes from entropy-attributed difference and history, and operation of distinct cognitive forms through commensuration, suspension, reopening, and return. It further connects these layers to research dynamics, organizational boundaries, port allocation, AI and institutional design, and a public specification for peace.

Major additions include the Scientific Ontology Concept Network, Truth Management and Boundary PDCA, Entropy-Attributed Difference and Cognitive Axis Formation, Optional Axiom Modules as a Cognitive Bridge, Cognitive Dynamics Communication Studies, Organizational Boundary and Port Model, and Specification for Peace.

The repository also strengthens its public governance infrastructure through concept-lineage metadata, public definition ownership, publication and commensuration policy, terminology collision registries, machine-readable document relationships, and public-format checking. The root README is an English-first, English/Japanese co-authoritative public interface; most research documents retain Japanese-authoritative and English-commensurated relations.

Scientific Ontology is a public conceptual framework for studying boundary, contact, history, cognition, communication, meaning, ethics, AI, organizations, social design, physics-adjacent correspondence, and return paths. It does not claim to replace established empirical sciences or to establish physical identity from cross-domain structural resemblance.
notes: This release extends boundary epistemological critique into boundary cognition formation, boundary cognition operation, research dynamics, organizational implementation, and peace specification. It remains a public conceptual research archive with explicit claim-strength, non-claim, terminology, and public/private boundaries.
